comment: Declarations a published TU publishes in its include/<unit>/<tu>.h before any published consumer uses them. Read by tools/header_harvest.py (published_exports); see docs/header-canon.md. An export never changes a spelling: it only counts as one more consumer of the owner's own declaration.

exports.reason: ov10/tu008 (src/ov10/cgp.c) owns the card game work area and declares CardGameWork in src/ov10/cgp.h. ov10/tu002 card_fread, tu003 and tu009 need its members, but none of them has published source yet, so the harvest has no consumer and include/ov10/cgp.h did not exist; their reworks include "ov10/cgp.h" instead of restating the type (review-bulk-r38 stage-04, orchestration notes FOLLOW-UP header-canon CardGameWork).

main/tu103 (src/main/xgl_packet.c) owns the VIF1 packet builder and completes struct XglPacket in src/main/xgl_packet.h; the accepted pool only forward-declares it (typedef struct XglPacket XglPacket; in include/shared.h). main/tu107 nmlPacketSetAttributeData/nmlPacketSetAttributeAlloc16N read and write XglPacket.cursor (+0x24) and were held until the owner publishes the body (review-bulk-r47 stage main/tu107, orchestration notes 'XglPacket owner layout'). A dereference is not an identifier the harvest can see, so the body is exported explicitly.

ov12/tu060 (src/ov12/rg_game_collision.c) owns the queued collision-check argument and declares RgGameColiArg (0x18 bytes: _CreateColiArg allocates sizeof(RgGameColiArg) and copies six words) in src/ov12/rg_game_collision.h. ov12/tu059 InitRgGeomGroupColiArg (0x00a30f08, still INCLUDE_ASM; validated bulk base) clears exactly those six words of the RgGameColiArg _CreateColiArg passes it, and review-bulk-r80 asked for RgGameColiArg * instead of a raw pointer, but tu059 has no published use of the type yet, so include/ov12/rg_game_collision.h did not exist (unblock-bulk-prep-20260919).

main/tu104 (src/main/xgl_studio.c) defines xglStudioGetCamera2 in C and declares it in its prelude as `extern StudioCamera *xglStudioGetCamera2(int camera_index);`, the spelling of the core decision in config/header-canon.json. Its published callers main/tu246 (src/main/camera.c through src/main/camera.h), main/tu116 (src/main/game.c) and main/tu100 (src/main/xgl_2.c) each redeclare the same prototype, so no TU uses the name undeclared and the layout never homed it in include/main/xgl_studio.h (the report's `math` entry is only the retired math view, withheld for StudioCamera, which include/shared.h now provides). Exported so those callers can include the definer's header instead of restating it (user-direct-fixes-20260919). Drop once a published caller uses the name without its own declaration.

ov12/tu065 (src/ov12/rg_filesys.c) defines RgFileSysDataGetName in C (published exact, ov12:0x00a34aa8) and declares it in src/ov12/rg_filesys.h with its definition's spelling. ov12/tu080 src/ov12/xrg_actor.c _DupLoadXenoActor calls it and redeclares the same prototype locally, so the layout had no undeclared consumer and include/ov12/rg_filesys.h did not exist. Exported so callers include the definer's header instead of restating it (user-direct-fixes-20260919). RgFileSysRead is still INCLUDE_ASM and is recorded in config/header-callees.json instead.

ov01/tu003 (src/ov01/battle_init.c) defines transWepIn/transWepOut in C on its own BattleUnit record and declares both in its prelude with the definition's spelling. ov01/tu002 src/ov01/unit_cmd.h restates them on its UnitRecord view, a TU-local divergence (docs/header-canon.md): that TU keeps its own declarations and does not include include/ov01/battle_init.h, so the definition wins in the definer's header and the umbrella withholds them (user-direct-fixes-20260919).

ov01/tu005 (src/ov01/data_unit_org_get.c) defines dataDefWpnGet in C as `int dataDefWpnGet(void *unit)` (it ignores the argument and returns 0) and declares it in src/ov01/data_unit_org_get.h with that spelling. ov01/tu002 (UnitRecord *) and ov01/tu003 (BattleUnit *) restate it on their own unit views, TU-local divergences that neither includes include/ov01/data_unit_org_get.h, so the definition wins in the definer's header and the umbrella withholds it (user-direct-fixes-20260919). dataMtdRead is still INCLUDE_ASM and has two incompatible caller spellings, so it is not registered.

ov12/tu023 (src/ov12/rg_shot.c) owns the shot essences and completes RgShotEssence (the prefix every shot kind shares: _InitShotCommon/_InitRgShotEssence) and RgNormalShotEssence (speed at +0x120, _CreateRgNormalShot/InitRgNormalShotEssence) in src/ov12/rg_shot.h. RgWeaponEssence.shotEssence (ov12/tu027, +0x10, stored by _ReadCommon at ov12:0x00a1d130) points at a shot-database entry, and ov12/tu006 _JobEnemy (ov12:0x00a0c918..0x00a0c92c) reads that entry's life (+0x08) and speed (+0x120) to estimate the shot's reach. tu006 has no published use of either type yet, so include/ov12/rg_shot.h carried RgHomingShotEssence without the RgShotEssence body it embeds and did not carry RgNormalShotEssence (shared-model-ov12-weapon-essence-20260925, user-authorized 2026-09-25).

ov12/tu054 (src/ov12/rg_geom_robot.c) defines `void RgGeomRobotSetDir(RgGeom *geom, RgVector direction)` at its mapped C function. The proposed defining-TU owner header src/ov12/rg_geom_robot.h contains that exact prototype. The retained ov12/tu015 candidate imports ov12/rg_geom_robot.h and calls RgGeomRobotSetDir, so the generated defining-TU header must export the provider declaration instead of requiring a block-scope declaration.
